name: NetBox
author: Netlens
description: Imports your documented network from NetBox (4.x): devices with a network role (router, switch, access point ...) become network nodes, every other device a client, and the cables between interfaces decide who hangs below whom, including the port a device is plugged into. Netlens matches them to what it finds on the network by MAC address, so the hierarchy shows your documentation. Read-only: it only sends GET requests with an API token that has read-only permissions.

info.title: Make a read-only API token
info.text: In NetBox: Admin > Users: make a user 'netlens' with only 'view' permissions on dcim and ipam objects (a permission with action View, objects dcim | device, dcim | interface, dcim | cable, ipam | ip address), then a token for that user with 'write enabled' off. Netlens only sees what the documentation has: a device without a MAC address on one of its interfaces cannot be matched and is skipped.

columns.label: API token
columns.help: NetBox 4.5+: the whole token as shown once, like nbt_<key>.<token>. Older NetBox: the 40 character token.

columns.label: Only these sites (slugs)
columns.help: Comma separated site slugs. Empty: all sites.

config.label: Network roles
config.default: router, firewall, gateway, switch, access-point, ap, wireless-ap
config.help: Comma separated device role slugs that count as network equipment (nodes). Every other device is a client. Roles named router, firewall or gateway become the gateway; switch becomes a switch; access-point, ap and wireless-ap an access point.
